_comment: Editorial narrative + triangulated level overrides for the 2026-08-10 session, delivered 2026-08-11. In normal operation `levels` is omitted and figures come live from FRED/Treasury; it is included here because this run had no market-data network access. Replace daily.
fund_flow_note: Positive — largest weekly inflow in over a month
notable_events: **Dovish rate repricing drove the tape.** After Friday's (Aug 7) weaker-than-expected July jobs report, the market leaned further into cuts; steady/lower belly yields gave credit risk a hospitable backdrop. Next FOMC is Sept 16 — July CPI (Aug 12) is the near-term swing factor.

**Primary market roared back on the reopen.** The high-grade market had its busiest issuance day in ~7 months (~19 IG issuers — utilities, overseas banks, Tyson Foods among them); dealers guided to ~$40bn for the week after ~$80bn last week. Heavy IG supply typically pulls HY syndicate desks along, with issuers rushing to print ahead of Wednesday's CPI.

**Technicals turned supportive.** HY retail fund flows flipped to their largest inflow in over a month, extending a decelerating-outflow trend; combined with solid Q2 earnings this underpinned a modest grind tighter in spreads.

**Spreads remain historically rich.** HY OAS in the mid-260s bps sits near multi-year tights (vs. ~233 bps June 2007, ~259 bps early 2025), leaving limited cushion and keeping the market sensitive to macro or idiosyncratic shocks.
outlook: **Positioning day into CPI.** Tue Aug 11 is largely a set-up session ahead of July CPI (Wed Aug 12, 8:30 ET). Expect HY firm-but-cautious with new-issue desks pushing deals out ahead of the print; a benign CPI supports a further grind tighter, a hot CPI is the main downside risk given thin spread cushion.
**Active primary slate likely** on any constructive open — refis and opportunistic prints ahead of CPI, echoing the busiest IG day since January.
**Rest-of-week catalysts:** PPI Thu Aug 13 (8:30 ET), Retail Sales Fri Aug 14 (8:30 ET), UMich prelim sentiment Fri (10:00 ET). FOMC not until Sept 16 — data, not the Fed, drives the week.

**Watch items:** (1) crude — further softness pressures the ~10%-of-index energy cohort; (2) idiosyncratic distress headlines in media/retail/healthcare (agencies flag elevated downgrade/default risk); (3) whether HY inflows persist, confirming the technical bid.
